text:
maria_sales: Neptune Health wants a hybrid POC. Requirements: run a lightweight agent inside their VPC, keep client source IPs visible in logs, strict egress allowlist (443 + 9000). They also want a short explanation of peering vs interface endpoints and an upfront ballpark for POC pricing.

neptune_ops: Confirmed constraints: no SNAT on traffic to us, only TLS ports allowed, vendor certs must be pinned and we must provide an audit trail.

jay_netops: Quick note: VPC Peering preserves client IPs end-to-end as long as routing points directly to our peered subnets. Interface endpoints (PrivateLink) create ENIs on our side; depending on setup we can preserve IPs but often we see translations unless we front with an EIP-based NAT/proxy.

eli_solutions: Tradeoffs to communicate:
- Peering: preserves src IP, needs route table updates and mutual CIDR non-overlap, simple firewall rules, better for strict network controls.
- PrivateLink: simpler from their firewall (allow SG to our ENI), easier for cross-account hosted setups, may require extra work to guarantee src IP preservation.

maria_sales: Neptune asked for a minimal checklist for their network/security teams and a single-line SOW item for each option. Can we sketch both?

jay_netops: Peering checklist (to send):
```
1) Confirm CIDR ranges do not overlap (customer: 10.80.0.0/16, us: 10.200.50.0/24)
2) Create VPC peering (accept from our account)
3) Add route: 10.200.50.0/24 -> peering connection in customer route tables
4) Security groups: allow outbound tcp 443,9000 to 10.200.50.0/24
5) Test using curl to our echo endpoint to validate X-Client-IP header
```

eli_solutions: PrivateLink SG snippet we can provide if they want fallback:
```
# on their side: allow outbound to our interface endpoint privatenet IPs
allow tcp 10.80.0.0/16 -> eni-xxxxxx port 443
allow tcp 10.80.0.0/16 -> eni-xxxxxx port 9000
```

neptune_ops: For failover they want primary peering and fallback to PrivateLink. Is that supported? How is routing prioritized?

jay_netops: Yes. We recommend route preference: set peering route at higher priority for normal ops, and configure a secondary route pointing to a NAT/proxy that targets our PrivateLink EIP pool. Alternatively use BGP/SD-WAN to steer. We'll include a short runbook for failover tests.

eli_solutions: Example test command for source IP verification (include in runbook):
```
# run from a host in customer VPC
curl -sS --resolve echo.redwood-inference.private:443:10.200.50.15 https://echo.redwood-inference.private/echo -k -H "Host: echo.test" | jq .headers.X-Client-IP
# expected: 10.80.x.x (their client IP)
```

tanvi_secteam: Security answers to include in questionnaire: cert pinning supported (we can provide SPKI fingerprints), customer-controlled KMS for keys at rest (Private deploy), logs can be forwarded to customer SIEM or retained in their VPC. We'll attach SOC2 and encryption docs.

maria_sales: Procurement wants a tiny pricing blurb for the SOW: peering + dedicated pool vs hosted+PrivateLink. Keep it short and non-binding.

eli_solutions: Draft SOW lines:
- Option A (Peering + Dedicated): Reserved instance fee + network egress at cost; recommended when client IP preservation and predictable latency/throughput are required.
- Option B (Hosted + PrivateLink): Pay-as-you-go per token + interface endpoint data transfer; simpler onboarding, useful as a fallback path.

neptune_ops: For the POC (6 weeks) they want cost estimate not a full quote. Can we provide a capped trial credit and a rough monthly delta?

maria_sales: I can offer a POC credit and a short non-binding delta estimate. Looping finance.

jay_netops: I'll draft the peering runbook, firewall snippets, and a small failover checklist (commands + expected outputs). Will post in this thread when done.

deploy-bot: task:create runbook-draft (peering + privatelink fallback) assigned to jay_netops  eta 3h

maria_sales: Thanks team. Jay/eli/tanvi  please get docs + snippets in doc form by EOD. Neptune needs to lock after legal review on Friday.

neptune_ops: Appreciated. If you can include the minimum IAM roles required for the customer to approve endpoints, that would speed approval.

jay_netops: Will add IAM least-privilege sample: EC2/VPC modify permissions limited to CreatePeeringConnection, AcceptPeeringConnection, CreateRoute, ModifyRouteTable, Describe*

eli_solutions: I'll assemble an options table (srcip preserved? complexity? recommended for POC?) and attach to SOW blurb.

maria_sales: Great. Upload when ready and I'll send to Neptune + procurement.
